title: RuneLite companion plugin sync payload
x-status-note: Provisional until a real RuneLite snapshot has validated against it (SDD §12.1, D12, plan step 8.5). Quest identity, the varbit-to-unlock-key mapping, diary and combat-achievement representation, and whether a *complete* bank scan is even detectable are facts about the RuneLite API that cannot be settled from the app side. Once reconciled the marker is removed and further changes require a payload_version bump under §12.2.
description: The single owner of the Java-to-Python seam (SDD §12.1). Python validates incoming payloads against this file; the Java plugin is written to match it. `additionalProperties: false` is set on every object in this schema, which is what makes §7.6's collection boundary a contract rather than a convention (G8): a payload carrying opponent names, chat, per-tick location, prayer selections or fight-time inventories is rejected by the schema itself.

payload_version.description: §12.2. A plain integer — there is no major/minor component. The server declares the set it understands (SUPPORTED_PAYLOAD_VERSIONS) and rejects anything outside it with 409.

observed_at.description: When the plugin took this snapshot. §4.5: observation time is not truth, so it is transmitted rather than assumed to be receipt time.

player.description: §6.1. Identity plus the two account-wide scalars §9.1's combat_level / quest_points leaves read.

username.description: The hiscores/WOM lookup key (§6.1). Also the only identity the server trusts — the payload carries no player_id, because an id supplied by the caller would be attacker-controlled (§6.11).

skills.description: §6.2. One entry per skill observed. Omitting a skill means 'not observed', which is not the same as level 1.

quests.description: §6.4. `in_progress` is not a positive state — §9.1 evaluates it `unsatisfied` (A5).

unlocks.description: §6.3, A12. Spellbook, achievement diaries and combat achievements ride here under the reserved `spellbook_` / `diary_` / `ca_` key prefixes — they get no field of their own, because a payload field with no table and no way to reference it from content would be a contract with no sink (§7.1).

observed_items.description: §6.5. Opportunistic sightings, never a continuous truth. Read together with `container_scans`, never alone.

container_scans.description: §6.5, the staleness anchor. A container that was scanned and found to hold nothing tracked MUST still appear here — that is the only thing distinguishing 'you do not own it' from 'we have never looked' (§4.5).

practice_events.description: §7.6, exactly the summarized shape and nothing more. The four properties below are the whole vocabulary: no opponent names, no attack sequences, no chat, no individual prayer selections, no fight-time inventories, no tick-by-tick location. `additionalProperties: false` on the item schema is what enforces that (G8).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant with an explicit offset. An offset-naive timestamp is rejected: every §4.5 comparison (`now - scanned_at`, `now - ended_at`) needs an aware instant, and guessing the zone is how a naive value becomes a silently wrong age. The pattern carries the constraint because `format` is annotation-only in JSON Schema and is not asserted by default.

content_key.description: An id authored in `content/` - lowercase snake_case, so a plugin-side key and a content-side key cannot differ by casing alone.

xp.description: §6.2, G5. `null` means unranked - never 0. A source that reports -1 for unranked normalizes it to null at its own adapter boundary (§7.3); -1 never reaches this contract, which is why `minimum` is 0.

status.description: §6.4. `unknown` is transmissible: the plugin may see a quest it cannot read state for, and that is a different fact from `not_started`.

state.description: §6.3. `available` means purchasable or attainable but NOT held - Rigour visible in the prayer book is not Rigour unlocked. §9.1 evaluates it `unsatisfied` (A5). The word reads as positive and is the single most likely place for a plugin author to go wrong.

scanned_at.description: When this container was last seen *in full* (§6.5). A partial view is not a scan.

domain.description: §7.6's six domains. A seventh is a code change, not a payload change (§10.8).

evidence_type.description: §6.7. A closed enum, not free text: an open string is where `opponent_dashboard_screenshot` eventually arrives. `lms_score_increased` is derived server-side from WOM (§7.6) and is deliberately absent - the plugin cannot observe it.
